candidates.evidence: https://www.mj.gov.tl/jornal/public/docs/2026/serie_1/SERIE_I_NO_11.pdf (read via pdftotext: art. 3-6, 18-19, 23, 26, Annex I form with kiosk/shop/warehouse types and micro/small size boxes); https://en.tatoli.tl/2026/03/16/timor-leste-launches-digital-system-to-strengthen-business-licensing-oversight/17/ (lic.mci.gov.tl launched; pre-inspections and periodic inspections).
candidates.existing: State online portal lic.mci.gov.tl (applicants can register, upload documents and get certificates online); SERVE counter. Local consultants were not found.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer and duty as K05 (2/10). New evidence the study may not have: the 6-month regularisation clock for existing firms, the mandatory vistoria with fire/health/local-authority team, and the state portal as a competitor. The start date set by the minister's despacho was not found; if it has been set, the deadline may fall in the next few months.
candidates.name: Sectoral commercial licence plus vistoria pack for existing medium/high-risk shops and warehouses
candidates.trigger: Decreto do Governo 3/2026 (Serie I No 11, 18 Mar 2026) under DL 89/2023 as amended by DL 5/2026: licence and prior inspection required at start, installation and alteration; existing companies must apply within 6 months of the start date for receiving applications (art. 23), which the minister fixes by despacho (art. 26). Renewal uses the same form. Inspections also happen ex officio.
candidates.unchecked: Date of the minister's despacho opening applications; list of activities classified medium/high risk in the DL 89/2023 annex; licence validity and fees; whether the lic.mci.gov.tl portal is mandatory and working; competitor search for private filing agents (the one run found none).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Kiosks and shops fall under the commercial licensing regime (kiosk is a listed establishment type in the Decreto 3/2026 form). Money transfer operators must report cash transactions of US$2,500 or more to the FIU (BCTL Instruction 01/2013); few operators.

coverage.found: Only through the commercial and industrial licensing regimes (DL 89/2023, DL 90/2023; Decreto 3/2026 and Decreto 4/2024), which require prior vistoria with a joint inspection team (commerce, local authority, health, fire service). Small food producers likely under the industrial regime. Not examined further.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: DL 1/2012 (downstream sector), Regulation 1/2013 (filling stations: location and project approval, inspection, fees), Regulation 1/2014 (fuel quality), all under ANPM. About 59 stations were contracted for the 2022 fuel subsidy. March 2026 Council of Ministers approved draft temporary fuel-price stabilisation measures (enactment unconfirmed). Few buyers.

coverage.found: DL 16/2004 on cooperatives. About 452 cooperatives (127 credit, 325 producer) per a Secretary of State statement in June 2023, over 118,000 members. No reporting duty or software gap confirmed. Weak candidate listed.

coverage.found: DL 18/2004 (private health unit licensing) and DL 14/2004 (professional registration), handled through the MoH Licensing Cabinet on TileSW. No insurer or state-scheme billing found; no national insurance scheme confirmed. Nothing actionable.

coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K10 (rejected). Not searched separately.

coverage.found: Private security sector described as largely unregulated in old sources (Small Arms Survey, a 2014 Mimbar Hukum paper); no 2024-2026 law found. Cleaning and manpower agencies not covered.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mineral law is DL 12/2021 under ANPM; 2008/2009 ministerial orders on quarry and sand extraction (current status unconfirmed); explosives licensed by the Ministry of Defence. No contractor registry or annual renewal text found. K07 already rejected (oil and gas).

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies

coverage.found: Medium and high-risk commercial establishments need a licence plus prior vistoria; applications go to SERVE counter, then Direcao-Geral do Comercio; renewal uses the same form. Art. 23: existing companies must apply within 6 months of the start date for receiving applications, which the minister sets by despacho (art. 26; the date was not found). MCI launched the online system lic.mci.gov.tl on 17 Mar 2026. Related to K05 (candidate listed as known).

candidates.evidence: https://mj.gov.tl/jornal/public/docs/2023/serie_1/SERIE_I_NO_48.pdf (read locally). Scrap wholesale 4669 and car parts 4530 are low risk, so these buyers only need declaration plus cadastro; 4662 metals wholesale is high risk. Same buyer group and duty as K05; adds the specific annual 31 January form as a recurring hook.
candidates.existing: None seen (no search for vendors; SERVE one-stop shop handles submission)
candidates.known_note: Same duty, same buyers. Adds evidence of a fixed annual deadline (31 Jan) and confirms scrap and parts dealers are low-risk, declaration-only. Not a revive trigger since K05 was never rejected.
candidates.name: Annual commercial-register update (31 Jan) and sectoral licence renewal for scrap, vehicle-parts and other small traders
candidates.trigger: DL 89/2023 art. 24-30: every commercial firm in Annexes I-III must enter the cadastro comercial and file an update form by 31 January each year for the previous year; registration is suspended if not filed. Medium/high-risk firms hold a 5-year sectoral licence (art. 6) renewed on the original file plus the old licence. Amended by DL 5/2026 (4 Feb 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the annual form is enforced in practice; the DL 5/2026 changes; annex wording after the amendment

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Read DL 89/2023 annexes (Jornal da Republica Serie I No 48, 20 Dec 2023, https://mj.gov.tl/jornal/public/docs/2023/serie_1/SERIE_I_NO_48.pdf). CAE 4669 'wholesale of waste, scrap and other products' is Annex I = LOW risk: no sectoral licence or prior inspection, only SERVE start-of-activity declaration plus mandatory entry in the commercial register (cadastro comercial) and an annual update form due 31 January (art. 23-30; suspension of registration if not filed). CAE 4662 'wholesale of ores and metals' is Annex III = HIGH risk (sectoral licence, 5-year validity, pre-inspection). Only scrap-specific rule found is a 2006 temporary ban on scrap collection, trade and export (https://etan.org/et2006/november/11/06export.htm); no current rule found, status unverified. No scrap-specific register or recurring report found. Folds into K05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No second-hand/pawn activity appears in DL 89/2023 Annexes I-III (checked for 'usad', 'penhor', 'antiguidade': none), so no specific licence found; they fall under the general commercial register. Pawn/lending: BCTL licenses non-deposit-taking 'finance companies' under Instruction 25/2023 (in force 21 Sep 2023; https://bancocentral.tl/en/news/go/publication-of-instruction-no-25-2023-of-july-4-on-the-licensing-and-supervision-of-finance-companies); whether pawn is covered is unverified. Few operators. Nothing new beyond K05.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Read DL 17/2026 (Serie I No 18, 6 May 2026, in force 30 days after publication): fee schedule for vehicle and driver acts. It lists import approval (A.I.V.I.), plates, vehicle inspection for registration, periodic vehicle inspection, goods-vehicle, hire-vehicle and passenger-transport licences, driving exams. No dismantler, scrap-vehicle or parts-trader item. Late filing is charged double. Fees are collected immediately by the competent body (art. 8); art. 5.2 allows concession for plate issue. Parts trade CAE 4530 (and motorcycle parts 4541) is Annex I LOW risk; vehicle repair 4520/4542 is Annex II MEDIUM risk (sectoral licence). No dismantler regime found. The transport-fleet angle (periodic inspection, licence renewals) belongs to cat. 18.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No registration, licence or recurring filing for beekeepers found. Honey is a donor/cooperative development topic only (SECoop and Bali Honey Madu agreement, Tatoli Sep 2025: https://en.tatoli.tl/2025/09/16/indonesia-to-help-timor-lestes-cooperatives-with-honey-produciton/00/). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No dedicated groundwater or driller licensing decree found. A 2022 Tatoli report quotes the Secretary of State for Environment saying a licence letter is required before drilling, tied to environmental licensing (DL 5/2011, amended by DL 39/2022; ANLA created by DL 41/2022; 2025 gazette text on A/B/C category fees, Serie I No 11A 2025). ANAS (DL 38/2020) is mandated to license water-resource use but no abstraction regulation or fee schedule found. Very few drillers; event-driven licence, not recurring. Related to cat. 33 environmental licensing fee decree from first pass. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: DL 2/2017 (urban solid waste system) puts collection and transport on municipal administrations. No septic-sludge hauler licence, manifest or register found. Category A/B/C environmental licensing (DL 5/2011 as amended) is the only regime and is project-based. Nothing new beyond the environmental-licensing item from first pass.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Timor-Leste lift, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection regime found; search returned only Portuguese and Brazilian law. Only possibly relevant item is Lei 11/2023 on occupational safety and health (Serie I No 15, 19 Apr 2023); text not read. Very few assets. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: DL 4/2004 lets communities run water supply through water management groups (GMF, Grupo de Gestao de Agua). ANAS (DL 38/2020) monitors and licenses water-supply operators, but a 2021 report says it had done little regulating. DL 5/2009 (Regulamento do Licenciamento, Comercializacao e Qualidade da Agua Potavel) requires approved source, licensing and lab testing for bottled water and for water supplied by tanker truck or network, with minimum sampling-frequency tables and fines of US$1,000 to US$10,000 (read locally via pdftotext). No evidence of enforced recurring reporting or of a software gap. GMFs are donor-supported (BESIK); low willingness to pay. See candidates.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No funeral or cemetery licensing law, register or fee schedule found in two searches (Portuguese and English). Burial is run by the church, family or municipality. Not in DL 89/2023 annexes. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations and foundations are governed by DL 5/2005 (non-profit legal persons), partly superseded by the Civil Code (Law 10/2011). Registration is described by a 2014 source as voluntary; 2019 EU report says FONGTIL then Ministry of Justice registration for NGOs, SECoop recognition for cooperatives. No annual report duty found. Halal: no Timor-Leste halal scheme found, only a 2023 Muhammadiyah recommendation (https://en.tatoli.tl/tag/muhammadiyah/28411). Muslim minority is tiny. Nothing new.
